newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Top Yugo bank slices lending rate to 3.25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Top Yugo bank slices lending rate to 3.25 pct.

text.p: Yugoslavia's largest commercial bank Beobanka cut on Monday its base lending rate to a monthly 3.25 percent, following a sharp reduction in the central bank's discount rate last week, the bank said.

"Respecting the National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) decision last week to cut its key discount rate to a monthly 2.5 from 4.5 percent, Beobanka's Board of Directors decided to cut its commercial lending rate to 3.25 from 5.85 percent per month," the bank said in a statement.
Yugoslav companies frequently cited high cost of borrowing as a major obstacle to increasing production and improving overall performance.
Beobanka said its latest move was a fresh relief to the capital-starved industry and was seen leading to an improved performance.
"The reduction in the base lending rate is also an additional effort by Beobanka to contribute to better financing of the forthcoming spring sowing," the statement said.
Unlike commercial lending rates, interest rates on the unofficial interbank dinar market range between 15 and 18 percent per month.

"The total cost of borrowing for companies will not exceed seven percent per month, including the entire banking commission and covering other costs of arranging the credit," Beobanka spokesman Zoran Pavlovic told Reuters. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
